page: Vultr vcg-a16-24c-256g-64vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with an Intel x86_64 processor offering 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. For accelerated workloads, it features four NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs with a combined total of 64 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 1200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show average performance across general compute and memory tasks, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1483.0 and a multi-core score of 13019.0. The system achieves a Passmark CPU score of 35340.23 and a multi-core stress-ng CPU performance of 41473.88. In memory-bound operations, it records a read-only large block bandwidth of 137.58 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 56.27 GB/sec. Notably, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in LLM prompt processing, reaching 8464.24 tokens/sec for a small 135M model and 614.8 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model. Text generation speeds are average for the small model at 253.1 tokens/sec and strong for the medium model at 32.83 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server bundles dense GPU resources and a high memory capacity, making it a viable option for multi-stream media processing, VDI, and moderate AI inference workloads without the premium cost of flagship enterprise compute GPUs. However, a key tradeoff is the CPU's moderate clock speed of 2.0 GHz and average single-core performance, which may limit performance in highly sequential, non-parallelized tasks. The server is configured for workloads such as LLM inference on small to medium models, image and video processing, ray tracing, and database operations requiring local NVMe storage.
